'''Robert John Hummel''' (born March 8, 1989) is an American professional [[basketball]] player and TV commentator. He played [[college basketball]] for [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue University]] and for the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in the [[NBA]]. In 2019, Hummel was named [[USA Basketball Male Athlete of the Year]]. He has served as an analyst for the [[Big Ten Network]] and [[Fox Sports]], and is a regular contributor for [[Westwood One Sports]] and [[SiriusXM]]. Robbie Hummel also works as a college basketball and [[NBA]] analyst for [[NBC Sports]] and [[CBS Sports]].

==High school career==
Hummel attended [[Valparaiso High School]] in [[Valparaiso, Indiana]]. Playing under coach Bob Punter, he played alongside his future college freshman teammate, Scott Martin (who transferred to the [[University of Notre Dame]] after one season at Purdue). Hummel averaged 15.7 points, 7.1 rebounds and 4.1 assists per game as a Viking during his senior season.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|url=http://www.purduesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/hummel_robbie00.html|title=Robbie Hummel Bio|work=PurdueSports.com|access-date=September 12, 2012|archive-date=July 22, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120722030905/http://www.purduesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/hummel_robbie00.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Hummel was listed as the No. 21 [[small forward]] and the No. 75 player in the nation in 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/40075|title=Robbie Hummel recruiting profile|work=Rivals.com|access-date=September 12, 2012}}</ref>

==College career==

===2007–2008===
Hummel attended [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue University]] to play under head coach [[Matt Painter]]. He averaged 11.4 points (second on team), 6.1 rebounds (first) and 2.5 assists a game in his freshman year. Hummel led the "Baby Boilers", along with [[Chris Kramer]], [[JaJuan Johnson]], Keaton Grant, and [[E'Twaun Moore]], to a second-place finish in conference play and on to a second-round [[2008 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] appearance, where they lost to a senior-led [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] team. He broke the school freshman record with a 44.7 three-point field goal percentage, while leading the [[Big Ten Conference]]. He also recorded the highest free throw percentage for a freshman in school history with 86.5 percent accuracy, which led the team, and broke [[Kyle Macy]]'s 33-year-old .859 mark. He was named First Team All-Big Ten, becoming the first true [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Boilermaker]] freshman to earn the honor. He finished his freshman season as one of 24 [[John R. Wooden Award]] finalists and of 10 finalists for the [[Oscar Robertson Trophy]]. He helped lead the Boilermakers to a 25–9 overall season record.<ref name="bio"/>

===2008–2009===
Hummel completed his [[2008–09 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|sophomore season]] averaging close to 13 points (3rd on team) and 7 rebounds (1st) a game. As one of three tri-captains on the team and named the Preseason Big Ten Player of the Year, he scored his 500th career point on December 13, 2008, against [[Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball|Indiana State]]. Hummel opened the season with ten straight double-figure-scoring performances, totaling 19 on the season (15–4), which included four 20-plus-point performances (3–1). He won back-to-back Big Ten Player of the Week honors in the month of December, pulling down a career-high 14 rebounds and scoring 25 points during that time frame. He recorded two preseason [[double-double]]s, with one coming against [[Stephen Curry]]'s [[Davidson Wildcats men's basketball|Davidson]] team. Hummel began battling with [[back spasms]] and a broken [[vertebra]], which forced him to sit out five games and kept him from practice involvement. He had to wear a [[back brace]] in games following with limited minutes, while helping lead the Boilermakers to an 11–7 conference record, going 1–3 without him. Hummel led the Boilermakers to their first [[2009 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]] championship in school history and was named the [[Big Ten men's basketball tournament|most outstanding player]] of the tournament, following with a third straight [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] appearance and the program's first [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|Sweet Sixteen]] appearance in 9 years. Finishing the season wearing a back brace, he scored a team high 17 points in the final game of the season against [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|UConn]] in the regional semifinals. Although having dealt with performance affecting injuries and missing four conference games, he was named a Third Team-All Big Ten selection.<ref name="bio"/>

===2009–2010===
[[File:20100123 Moore, Johnson and Hummel at a press conference.jpg|thumb|left|[[E'Twaun Moore]], [[JaJuan Johnson]] and Hummel at press conference (January 23, 2010)]]
To start the [[2009–10 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|2009–10 season]], Hummel was picked as one of fifty players as a preseason [[John R. Wooden Award]] candidate, along with teammate, E'Twaun Moore. He was a Preseason First Team All-Big Ten pick by both [[CBS Sports]] and [[Big Ten Network]] and a Preseason 2nd Team All-American pick by [[ESPN]] analysts, [[Doug Gottlieb]] and [[Jay Williams (basketball)|Jay Williams]]. Near mid-season, he was selected as one of thirty finalists for the [[Naismith Award]]. With MVP [[E'Twaun Moore]], Hummel was named to the 2009 [[Paradise Jam]] All-Tournament Team after a victory over #10 [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]]. During a school record-tying 14–0 season start on December 29, 2009, against [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]], Hummel broke a school record, making 36 consecutive free throws, previously held by [[Jerry Sichting]]'s 34, which was set three decades earlier. He tied his former assistant coach, [[Cuonzo Martin]]'s single-game school record of 8 three-point field goals made in a losing effort against an [[Evan Turner]]-led [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] team on January 12, 2010, in which he also scored a career high 35 points and received a dislocated [[pinky finger]]. In his team's tenth straight win in conference play at [[Minnesota Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] on February 24, Hummel injured his right knee in the first half after he slipped while attempting to plant his foot. He scored 11 points, making 3-of-4 three-pointers, in his prior twelve minutes of the game. Purdue officials reported the following day that Hummel [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|tore]] his [[anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL) and would miss the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=4946559 |title=Purdue loses Hummel for season |work=ESPN.com |date=February 25, 2010 |access-date=March 22, 2010}}</ref> He finished the last five games as a junior perfect from the free throw line, making all 21 of his attempts.<ref name="bio"/>

Playing 30.3 minutes per game, he averaged 15.7 points (2nd on team), 6.9 rebounds (1st), 1.1 steals, 1 block, and 2.1 assists, while shooting 45.6 percent from the floor and led the Big Ten at 90.2 percent from the line, while also leading the nation amongst players at the forward position. He also shot 36.4 percent beyond the arc (2nd). Hummel scored at least 11 points in all but three games on the season (24–3), including ten straight, while recording eight double-doubles and being named a First Team All-Big Ten selection for the second time in his career at Purdue, while also being named a [[Fox College Sports|Fox Sports]] Third-Team All-American, a [[State Farm]] and [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] Second Team All-American, and an [[Associated Press]] Honorable Mention All-American. He averaged 16.2 points and 7.3 rebounds per game in Big Ten Conference play for the third-ranked team in the nation (12–3). Hummel received knee surgery and had to wait 4 to 6 months for the healing process.<ref name="bio"/>

===2010–2011===
After two consecutive seasons with performance-affecting injuries, Hummel was expected to return for his senior season. Fellow teammates JaJuan Johnson and E'Twaun Moore were returning as well, where they pulled out of the [[2010 NBA draft]] to return for their senior season.  At team practice on October 16, Hummel tore the same ACL and was forced to sit out and serve as an assistant for the 2010–11 season. Before the injury, Hummel was predicted as high as a Preseason Second Team All-American by much of the media.<ref name="bio"/>

===2011–2012===
Hummel returned to the team as a fifth-year [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] senior. On October 19, 2011, he showed no effects from his injury during 3-on-3 fast-break drills in practice. Hummel was named one of 50 candidates for the [[John R. Wooden Award]], as well as the #24 player on [[CBSSports.com]] Top 100 List and a Lowe's [[Senior CLASS Award]] candidate to open the season. On November 11, the Preseason All-Big Ten selection scored 21 points, making 5-of-7 beyond the arc to open the season against [[Northern Illinois Huskies|Northern Illinois]] in 20 minutes of play. On December 3 in a three-point loss at #11 [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]], Hummel suffered from [[cramp]]s and [[dehydration]], which eventually caused him to fall to the floor in the last minute of the game. Hummel led Purdue to a 10–3 non-conference mark and onto a 10–8 conference record. Hummel led the Boilermakers with 16.4 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 1.2 blocks per contest, while averaging 2 assists and .7 steals. He scored in double figures in all but three games (1–2) this season, which included nine 20-plus-point games (7–2), while recording six double-doubles (4–2). On February 4, Hummel recorded a career-high 5 blocks in a home loss to #20 [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]]. On February 22, he scored a season-high 29 points in a home win against [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]]. Following that game and a 17-point performance win at #11 [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]], Hummel was named Big Ten Player of the Week. In his last game at [[Mackey Arena]] on February 29, Hummel recorded a career-high 6 assists, along with 26 points and 8 rebounds against [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State]]. Throughout the month of February, Hummel led the nation in points scored. After the culmination of the regular season, Hummel was selected First Team All-Big Ten for the third time in his career, becoming the first Boilermaker since [[Rick Mount]] (1968–1970) to do so and the first Big Ten player since [[Mateen Cleaves]]. Hummel led the Boilermakers to a sixth straight NCAA tournament, losing in his final game to Final Four-bound [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] in the third round by 3 points. Being guarded by [[Thomas Robinson (basketball)|Thomas Robinson]], Hummel scored 22 points in the first half, finishing with 26 points and 9 rebounds. He was named an [[Associated Press]] Honorable Mention All-American and also won the Lowe's [[Senior CLASS Award]] and the Thomas A. Brady Comeback Award.<ref name="bio"/>

===Career notes===
Hummel became the 44th player in school history to score over 1,000 career points, surpassing the mark with a 13-point performance during a 73–66 loss on January 9, 2010. On December 23, 2011, at [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]], Hummel became the tenth player in school history to tally 700 rebounds. His 90.2 free throw percentage on the [[2009–10 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|2009–10 season]] ranks second best in school history. On March 4, 2012, with a 16-point performance in a loss at Indiana, Hummel scored his 1,720th career point, placing him ninth in career points at Purdue. He finished his career with 1,772 points (9th), 862 rebounds (4th), 268 assists, 132 steals, 112 blocks, becoming the only Boilermaker to reach such numbers in each category.<ref name="bio"/>

==Professional career==
[[File:Real Madrid-Obradoiro Santiago mayo 2013CCropedhummel80919.jpg |thumb|Hummel in 2013 for [[Obradoiro CAB]]]]
On June 28, 2012, Hummel was selected by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] with the 58th overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Remme |first=Mark |date=June 28, 2012 |title=Wolves Select Purdue's Robbie Hummel With 58th Pick In 2012 NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/wolves-select-purdues-robbie-hummel-58th-pick-2012-nba-draft |access-date=October 29, 2016 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> In July 2012, he joined the Timberwolves for the 2012 NBA Summer League.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kduz.com/2012/07/16/wolves-announce-2012-nba-summer-league-roster/|title=WOLVES ANNOUNCE 2012 NBA SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER|work=KDUZ.com|date=July 16, 2012|access-date=October 29, 2016|archive-date=October 30, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161030074908/http://www.kduz.com/2012/07/16/wolves-announce-2012-nba-summer-league-roster/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On August 8, 2012, Hummel signed a one-year deal with [[Obradoiro CAB|Blu:sens Monbús]] of Spain.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/94305/obradoiro-officially-signs-wolves-draftee-robbie-hummel.html|title=Obradoiro officially signs Wolves draftee Robbie Hummel|work=Sportando.com|date=August 8, 2012|access-date=August 8, 2012}}</ref> In September 2012, he injured his right meniscus and was sidelined for two months.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/95190/obradoiro-robbie-hummel-to-miss-4-to-8-weeks.html|title=Obradoiro, Robbie Hummel to miss 4-to-8 weeks|work=Sportando.com|date=September 12, 2012|access-date=September 12, 2012}}</ref>

In July 2013, Hummel re-joined the Minnesota Timberwolves for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://minnesota.cbslocal.com/2013/07/09/timberwolves-announce-2013-summer-league-roster/|title=Timberwolves Announce 2013 Summer League Roster|work=CBSLocal.com|date=July 9, 2013|access-date=October 29, 2016}}</ref> On September 26, 2013, he signed with the Timberwolves,<ref>{{cite web |date=September 26, 2013 |title=Wolves Sign Brown, Hummel And Jeffers To Camp Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-sign-brown-hummel-and-jeffers-camp-roster |access-date=September 26, 2013 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> and he re-signed with them on July 22, 2014.<ref>{{cite web |date=July 22, 2014 |title=Timberwolves Re-Sign Forward Robbie Hummel |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-re-sign-forward-robbie-hummel |access-date=July 22, 2023 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> On January 26, 2015, he was ruled out indefinitely after suffering a non-displaced fracture of the fourth metacarpal in his right hand.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/robbie-hummel-injury-update|title=ROBBIE HUMMEL INJURY UPDATE|work=NBA.com|date=January 26, 2015|access-date=January 26, 2015}}</ref>

On June 28, 2015, the Timberwolves tendered a qualifying offer to make Hummel a restricted free agent.<ref>{{cite web|first=Andy|last=Greder|url=http://www.twincities.com/2015/06/27/timberwolves-make-offer-to-robbie-hummel/|title=Timberwolves make offer to Robbie Hummel|work=TwinCities.com|date=June 27, 2015|access-date=June 27, 2015}}</ref> However, they later withdrew the offer on July 6, thus parting ways with him.<ref>{{cite web|first=Chuck|last=Myron|url=http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2015/07/wolves-pull-qualifying-offer-to-robbie-hummel.html|title=Wolves Pull Qualifying Offer To Robbie Hummel|work=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 6, 2015|access-date=July 6, 2015}}</ref>

On July 31, 2015, Hummel signed a one-year deal with Italian team [[Olimpia Milano|EA7 Emporio Armani Milano]].<ref>{{cite news|title=EA7 Milan signs power forward Hummel|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/68ltn6glb9nrdshq|access-date=July 31, 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=July 31, 2015}}</ref> On February 5, 2016, he parted ways with Milano, after suffering a serious shoulder injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/190081/robbie-hummel-olimpia-milano-part-ways.html|title=Robbie Hummel, Olimpia Milano part ways|work=Sportando.com|date=February 5, 2016|access-date=February 5, 2016}}</ref> He appeared in 11 games and had four starts in the Italian League, averaging 9.0 points and 5.0 rebounds in 22.4 minutes per game. He also played in nine games while having one start in Euroleague play, averaging 7.6 points, 4.0 rebounds and 1.0 assists per game.<ref name="Nuggets">{{cite web |date=September 15, 2016 |title=Nuggets Sign Four Players to Contracts |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-four-players-to-contracts-091516 |access-date=September 16, 2016 |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}</ref>

On September 15, 2016, Hummel signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]],<ref name="Nuggets"/> but was waived on October 22 after appearing in seven preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=19841|title=Nuggets waive Nate Wolters and Robbie Hummel|work=InsideHoops.com|date=October 22, 2016|access-date=October 22, 2016}}</ref> Seven days later, he signed with Russian club [[BC Khimki|Khimki]] for the rest of the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://en.bckhimki.ru/news/clubnews/2016/october/1145/|title=BC KHIMKI SIGNED WITH ROBBIE HUMMEL|work=BCKhimki.ru|date=October 29, 2016|access-date=October 29, 2016}}</ref>

==International career==
With his lower back injury healing daily, Hummel was selected for the USA Men's [[2009 Summer Universiade|2009]] [[World University Games]] in [[Belgrade]], Serbia under [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]] head coach [[Bo Ryan]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Griffiths |first=Doug |date=June 18, 2009 |title=Hummel in, Johnson out at World University Games |url=https://collegebasketball.rivals.com/content.asp?SID=1146&CID=957540 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160329154950/https://collegebasketball.rivals.com/content.asp?SID=1146&CID=957540 |archive-date=March 29, 2016 |access-date=June 18, 2009 |work=Rivals.com}}</ref> Along with the likes of fellow Big Ten players [[Evan Turner]] and [[Talor Battle]], Hummel helped lead Team USA to the Bronze medal against [[Israel]], finishing with a 6–1 record.<ref>{{cite web |last=Oren |first=Paul |date=July 12, 2009 |title=Hummel earns bronze medal with Team USA |url=http://www.nwitimes.com/sports/local/hummel-earns-bronze-medal-with-team-usa/article_bf82bc20-54eb-5486-bcab-30b560aeaaed.html |access-date=July 12, 2009 |work=NWI.com}}</ref> Pulling down a team single-game-high ten rebounds, he averaged 7.3 points and 3.4 rebounds per game.

==Retirement and 3x3 career==
On October 4, 2017, Hummel announced he was retiring from professional basketball in order to become a studio analyst and color commentator for [[ESPN]] and [[Big Ten Network]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/purdue/2022/01/19/robbie-hummel-espn-big-ten-network-jason-benetti-college-basketball-analysts-purdue-boilermakers/6568333001/ | publisher=IndyStar.com | title=How Robbie Hummel became one of college basketball's best TV analysts | author=Matthew VanTryon | date=January 19, 2022 | access-date=February 15, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2017/10/04/former-purdue-star-robbie-hummel-retires-playing-begin-broadcasting/730299001/|title=Former Purdue star Robbie Hummel retires from playing to begin broadcasting
|first=Nathan|last=Baird|work=[[Journal & Courier]]|publisher=[[USA Today]]|date=October 4, 2017|access-date=December 25, 2018}}</ref> In 2017, Hummel signed a three-year broadcasting contract with multiple networks followed by a two-year deal with the same. Following the Big Ten's signing of a new media deal that included NBC and Fox and left out ESPN, Hummel signed with the two former networks and left the latter.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/indiana/big-ten/robbie-hummel-leaving-espn-for-nbc-fox-big-ten-network |title=Purdue Legend Robbie Hummel Leaving ESPN for NBC, Fox |date=September 25, 2023 }}</ref>

Hummel is a regular contributor on [[Westwood One Sports]]<ref>{{cite web|url= https://westwoodonesports.com/ |access-date=28 August 2023 |title=Westwood One Sports}}</ref> as well as [[SiriusXM]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Sirius XM |url=https://www.siriusxm.com/homepage?adobe_mc_sdid=SDID%3D1A8CB8878E998AD7-1FF8B1BC189EF76A%7CMCORGID%3DAA6F3BC75245B3970A490D4D%40AdobeOrg%7CTS%3D1668571200 |access-date=August 27, 2023}}</ref>

=== 3x3 career ===
In 2019, Hummel joined Team Princeton 3X3 on the [[FIBA 3x3 World Tour]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://worldtour.fiba3x3.com/2018/teams/0d533869-0f99-4a2a-b0d8-3bd758377969|title=Princeton {{!}} FIBA 3x3 World Tour 2018|website=worldtour.fiba3x3.com|access-date=2019-04-08}}</ref> On June 23, 2019, Hummel won a gold medal at the [[2019 FIBA 3x3 World Cup]] in Amsterdam.

== Personal life ==
In 2023, Hummel became engaged to actress Logan Andrews after proposing in the Bahamas.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Leistikow |first=Chad |title=Leistikow: Announcer Robbie Hummel is seemingly everywhere at once as March Madness begins |url=https://www.hawkcentral.com/story/sports/college/2025/03/04/robbie-hummel-tv-broadcaster-college-basketball-march-madness-fox-ncaa-tournament/80381928007/ |access-date=2026-05-19 |website=Hawk Central |language=en-US}}</ref>
